claims: A rib contusion (bruised rib) is a painful injury caused by a direct blow or fall that damages the muscles, cartilage, or bone periosteum.
A rib contusion causes tenderness and swelling.
Pain from a rib contusion is usually intense when breathing deeply, coughing, or moving.
Treatment for a rib contusion focuses on pain management, breathing exercises, and rest.
A rib contusion typically heals in 3–6 weeks.
A rib contusion causes sharp pain with breathing, laughing, sneezing, or twisting.
Swelling and pain directly over the affected area, with or without visible bruising.
A rib contusion causes difficulty taking deep breaths, causing a sensation of chest tightness.
Doctors often use physical exams and patient history to diagnose a rib contusion.
X-rays may be used to rule out fractures in rib contusion diagnosis.
Minor fractures often appear the same as rib contusions and are treated identically.
Pain from a rib contusion improves within a few days.
Full recovery from a rib contusion can take 3 to 6 weeks.
Holding a pillow against the ribs while coughing can reduce pain.
